title: PACTEL ATWS-10 independent pressurizer insurge/outsurge experiment

source.title: NUREG/IA-0231: An Assessment of TRACE V4.160 Code Against PACTEL ATWS-10-13 and ATWS-20-21 Pressurizer Experiments
source.author: E. Takasuo
source.publisher: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission / VTT Processes
source.sourceKind: Measured separate-effects test pressure published by the experimental facility's research organization; the adjacent TRACE curve is not used as measurement.
source.redistribution: Only extracted numerical facts and original extraction code are distributed. The report PDF, figure artwork, prose, and TRACE input deck are not bundled or relicensed.

supplementaryFacilitySource.title: General description of the PACTEL test facility, VTT Research Notes 1929
supplementaryFacilitySource.facts: Section 2.2.4 independently gives the 8.8 m height, 139.7 mm inner diameter and 7.77 m surge line with 27.3 mm inner diameter. Table A.3 (PDF page 85, printed A50) lists 133.5 litres pressurizer volume and 153.3 cm² flow area. The ideal cylindrical volume used by the IA-0231 input is 134.8854 litres; do not silently replace one with the other.

experiment.facility: PACTEL, Lappeenranta University of Technology, Finland
experiment.type: Separate-effects pressurizer insurge followed by outsurge
experiment.independence: Different facility, date and experiment from the Krško 2005 operating-plant transient. No PACTEL pressure samples may be used to calibrate model coefficients.
experiment.developmentUse: The report's mechanistic discussion informs model development. This is an independent event comparison, not a blind validation holdout. Fix parameters from cited dimensions, properties and correlations before the first comparison; do not tune them automatically to this pressure trace.
experiment.timeConvention: The experiment starts at t=0. Use the printed times unchanged; do not shift the curve to align its peak with a boundary event.
experiment.originalAcquisitionPeriodNote: The source does not state the measurement acquisition interval. Its 0.5 s output interval refers to TRACE graphics output, not measurement acquisition.

operatorEvents.event: Insurge stops; draining starts; facility core power switched off

experiment.operatorEventBasis: Table 2, printed page 7, PDF page 11. Core power maintains the external facility water temperature and is not a direct pressurizer heater input.

extraction.method: Decode the sole embedded RGB image on PDF page 17 using pypdf; retain only the red Pactel measurement path below the legend, reject black dashed TRACE pixels, and linearly resample the per-column median red-path height.
extraction.redSelection: R>=240 and R-G>=50 and R-B>=50; plot rows 130..634 exclude the legend. Multiple disjoint red branches in a column are rejected.
extraction.resamplingNote: The 1 s grid is a reading grid, not the unknown instrument acquisition grid. Six decimal places support byte reproducibility, not measurement precision.
extraction.allowanceBasis: A conservative two-pixel allowance in each axis. It is a graphical extraction allowance, not a stochastic instrument uncertainty. Boundary timing and digitization error are kept distinct.
extraction.endpointPolicy: Discard 0-4 s and 496-500 s; no extrapolation or invented endpoint measurements.

measuredInitialConditions.basis: Table 1, printed page 6, PDF page 10; geometry in section 2.2 and Figure 2.

publishedBoundaryModel.classification: Numeric boundary approximation from the report's TRACE input appendix; these are not raw instrument histories.
publishedBoundaryModel.basis: Appendix A-3/A-4 (PDF pages 28/29) and A-8/A-9 (PDF pages 33/34). Section 3 states the outsurge is the measured average flow, rather than a fitted discharge-orifice result.
publishedBoundaryModel.interpolation: Piecewise linear between published knots; hold the terminal value after the final knot.
publishedBoundaryModel.surgeSignConvention: Positive enters the pressurizer through its liquid region; negative removes liquid. Incoming enthalpy must not be used for outgoing liquid.
publishedBoundaryModel.inletTemperatureBasis: FILL tlin, Appendix A-3. Nearly saturated injection is described in section 2.2.1; the exact 547 K is a published calculation input, not an independently tabulated instrument measurement.
publishedBoundaryModel.temperatureBasis: Liquid/vapor initialization in Appendix A-3; wall initialization in A-7. These are TRACE setup values, not additional measured response channels.
publishedBoundaryModel.wallDimensionsBasis: Figure 2 gives pipe OD 168.3 mm and thickness 14.3 mm; Appendix A-7 gives inner/outer radii explicitly.
publishedBoundaryModel.wallMaterialBasis: Figure 2 parts list identifies vessel pipe item 1 as AISI 304 (heaters item 2 are AISI 316L). TRACE MATRD=6 appears in Appendix A-7. The report does not tabulate density, conductivity or heat-capacity functions; a surrogate must declare its own documented assumptions for them.
publishedBoundaryModel.heatLossBasis: Section 3.1 says 3.44 W/(m²K) was evaluated from facility heat loss; Appendix A-6 applies 3.44 and 298 K at the outer wall. The prose rounds ambient temperature to 25°C.

measurementUncertainty.basis: Section 4.1, printed page 13/PDF page 16, gives the maximum pressure-measurement error for this test and states it also applies to the other tests.
measurementUncertainty.distribution: Unspecified. Treat as a reported error bound, not one standard deviation.
measurementUncertainty.conditionalEnvelopeBasis: Arithmetic sum of the reported 0.094 MPa pressure error bound and the separate 0.0142857 MPa two-pixel reading allowance. Apply the separate ±1.20048 s graphical time allowance when reporting conditional coverage. This is not a statistical confidence interval or a complete uncertainty budget.
measurementUncertainty.flowNote: The ±0.000793 kg/s spray-flow error in section 4.6 belongs to ATWS-21. It must not be transferred to the ATWS-10 insurge or outsurge.

calibrationAndHoldout.parameterFitting: No pressure response values calibrate geometry, wall heat capacity, heat-transfer coefficients, phase transfer, mixing, or timing. Do not optimize against this curve.
calibrationAndHoldout.acceptance: This is a conditional component comparison. Report raw discrepancies and the separately stated measurement/reading bounds. Unknown input and model uncertainties prevent a blanket plant-validation pass.

limitations: PACTEL is a small pressurizer experiment for a volume-scaled VVER-440 facility, not a 1000 MWe PWR operating-plant transient. It tests pressure physics and does not validate the coupled power plant.
Measured pressure is a digitized figure rather than the original acquisition dataset; no calibration file or original measurement timestamps are supplied.

The 491 resampled positions are correlated readings along one plotted curve, not 491 independent raw instrument samples. Coverage percentages and RMSE are descriptive comparisons, not confidence levels.
Flow and temperature forcing uses the published study's boundary approximation. Continuous measured flow, inlet temperature and heater electrical-power histories are unavailable in the report.
Only pressure is held out. Wall/fluid temperature and level response curves are not supplied by this report for independent scoring.
The Table 1 pressure 5.9 MPa and Figure 5 pre-event trace near 5.86 MPa differ slightly; both are preserved without offset correction.
Figure 5 reaches its measured peak near 219 s, while Table 2 stops insurge at 221 s. No time shift or boundary timing adjustment is made to hide this difference.
The reported wall heat-loss coefficient is a facility estimate; its uncertainty and temperature dependence are not specified.
A lumped implementation omits the published surge-line inventory, hydrostatic distribution and axial/radial wall temperature fields unless those effects are modeled explicitly.

The chosen cylindrical geometry follows IA-0231's published benchmark input. The independent facility description lists 133.5 litres rather than the ideal cylinder's 134.885 litres; actual surge-line geometry also differs from the simplified input. This geometry approximation is preserved and disclosed rather than fitted to pressure.
The report's general text describes injection after 100 s; the case-specific measured operator table and published boundary table put ATWS-10 insurge at 120 s. Use the case-specific times.
